summary.name: writui
summary.one_liner: A terminal writing app for Markdown that stores posts locally in a password-encrypted vault.
use_cases: writing blog posts in a terminal
keeping multiple versions of a draft
exporting posts to a blog or another editor
summary.what_it_does: Writui is a terminal-based writing app with a single calm column that formats Markdown as you type while keeping the Markdown marks visible. It saves writing automatically and restores your cursor position when you reopen a post. Posts are stored on your computer in a password-encrypted vault that can be locked and unlocked with Touch ID. You can save named versions of a draft before editing and read or restore them later. It also supports importing Markdown or text files and copying or exporting writing as Markdown. Install is via a curl script on macOS or Linux, and it is free and open source.
notable: Password-encrypted local vault with Touch ID unlock
Named draft versions that can be read or restored
Markdown formatting as you type with marks still visible
Installs with a single curl command; upgrade via writui upgrade
caveats: No prebuilt Windows install; Windows users must build from source
Touch ID unlock is tied to macOS
